claim_summary: STRIDE trains a student LLM to produce forecasting reasoning and projects its hidden-state prior into a TSFM for jointly reasoned numerical forecasts.

claim_evidence.quote: In summary, our contributions are three folds: (i) a Novel Cross-Modal Framework that utilizes a generalized latent projection mechanism to natively inject LLM reasoning into TSFM embedding spaces, entirely bypassing discrete token bottlenecks; (ii) a Reasoning Distillation Pipeline enabling a lightweight student LLM to generate high-quality analytical strategies using strictly historical context

modules.name: Cross-modal latent projection and fusion
modules.scope_reason: R2 places the trainable projection and latent fusion on the LLM side because it changes how temporal inputs and model representations are aligned; the R3 Harness layer test is not applicable because this is part of the jointly trained model, not an around-model runtime module.

evidence.quote: A trainable linear projection matrix 𝑊𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑗 maps ℎ𝑅 to the exact dimensionality of the target TSFM,

modules.name: Student LLM reasoning distillation
modules.scope_reason: R2 places the causal-language-model supervision and LoRA updates on the LLM side because they train the model to generate forecasting analyses; the R3 Harness test is not applicable because no runtime action-selection procedure is trained.

evidence.quote: Next, we distill this reasoning capability into a lightweight student LLM. Crucially, while the teacher utilizes 𝑌 and E to generate 𝑅𝑟𝑒𝑓, the student is tasked with predicting equivalent analytical insights relying strictly on the historical context 𝑋.

modules.name: Oracle reasoning training corpus
modules.scope_reason: R2 includes training data built to train an LLM capability; the R3 Harness test is not applicable because this corpus supervises model-side reasoning rather than implementing a runtime workflow or task verifier.

evidence.quote: First, we construct a high-quality reference reasoning dataset using the training splits of the GIFT-Eval (Aksu et al., 2024), partitioning sampled temporal windows into a historical context 𝑋 and a pseudo-future ground truth 𝑌.

temporal_validity.quote: To avoid any seen data or leakage issue for in-domain evaluation on TFRBench, we excluded the samples, which are used during training of our framework.

task_performance.quote: As illustrated in Figure 2, our approach establishes a new state-of-the-art, securing the top performance across both deterministic and probabilistic metrics. Specifically, our framework achieves a Mean Absolute Scaled Error (MASE) of 0.674 and a Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) of 0.454.

notes: Three model-side contributions are identified: the cross-modal projection/fusion, student reasoning distillation, and a separately constructed oracle reasoning dataset. No Harness module is contributed.
